_comment: Company-specific editorial policy for scripts/lint_article.py and scripts/build_orchestrator_review.py. Example Co is a fictional company: every rule below is invented to show how detailed such rules need to be. Replace the content of each block with your own product rules (knowledge/positioning.md); the scripts keep only the writing-craft rules and the mechanics (clause splitting, attribution to the brand, negation, table rows, intro zone). Patterns are Python regular expressions, compiled case-insensitively unless a rule says otherwise. `brand` is the public brand name exactly as it is written in prose, `product` is the product name, `site_host` is the bare host of the site (internal links). `self_reference_nouns` are the noun phrases an article uses for the company inside its own card (“The platform keeps…”); the pronouns it / we are built in.

banned_topics._comment: Topics the site never covers, in any field and in any form. The rule does not depend on whether the statement is true: a banned topic can reach an article simply because it is a published feature of the vendor the article is about. Checked on every line outside code blocks, including image alt and title text.

rules.message: visa sponsorship and immigration advice are outside the blog's scope in any form

site_wide_wording._comment: House wording rules applied to every line outside code blocks, whoever the sentence is about. `case_sensitive: true` compiles the pattern without the ignore-case flag (needed for the abbreviation rule).

rules.message: “only product” is internal wording and is not written publicly: use the category formula and the product name
abbreviations are written in upper case: AOR, EOR

industry_term_not_a_label._comment: An industry term that may describe how an arrangement works but is never the company's own label or product name. A scheme word right after the term (“works on an agent of record model”) marks a description of the arrangement and is allowed; the term next to the brand without such a word is a label and is blocked. The window ends at a full stop and at a table-cell border, because neighbouring cells of a comparison row speak about different vendors.
industry_term_not_a_label.message: “Agent of Record” is not an Example Co label: describe the company with the category formula from positioning.md, the product is Example Workspace; describing an arrangement is fine (“works on an agent of record model”)

self_forbidden._comment: Claims blocked only in a clause attributable to the brand: a sentence that names it, a continuation of such a sentence (“It …”, “and offers …”), its own H2–H4 section, its own table row. About the market and competitors the same words are ordinary facts. A negated clause (“is not a marketplace”) is a permitted boundary statement, not a claim. `kind` names the rule group; build_orchestrator_review.py lists denials of the `label` group for the coordinator. “Employer of record” is deliberately absent from the labels: “Example Co and an employer of record” is an ordinary contrast, and employer of record as a label for Example Co is checked by QA.

rules.message: speed claim (at most “in a few steps”)
label of a marketplace, staffing agency, law firm, legal adviser or payment provider
retired category wording; the current formula is in positioning.md
guarantee (write “helps keep contractor documents in order”)
superlative without a public source (best, leading, number one)
price adjective (the price is quoted verbatim from positioning.md)
customer count or growth figure that the site does not publish

negation_paraphrases._comment: The one negation permitted in copy is “not an employer of record”. Longer paraphrases of it are not used; they are blocked in a line that names the brand or the product and inside the brand's own section. A sentence about the market (“a payroll provider does not become the employer”) is not touched.
patterns: \b(?:is never|never becomes|never acts as) (?:the|an?|anyone['’]?s?) (?:legal |formal )?employer\b(?! of record)
negation_paraphrases.message: wording withdrawn by the publisher: “not an employer of record” is enough

classification_guarantee._comment: Software does not decide a worker's legal status. Blocked in a line that names the brand and inside the brand's own section; about the market the same words are ordinary subject matter.
classification_guarantee.message: the software does not decide a worker's legal status: the facts of the engagement and the applicable law do (write “keeps the documents that show how the engagement is set up”)

self_negation_intro._comment: Do not open with what the company is not. In the intro zone (everything before the second H2: the title and the key takeaways) a negation about the brand reads as a defence; in the vendor card and in an honest-limit cell of the summary table it is in its place. `subjects` are the sentence openers that continue a line about the brand.

reference_manner._comment: Manner of the site's published articles that passed the editor and rank; the linter prints an article's numbers next to these and never blocks on them. Densities are per 1,000 words of prose, never absolute counts: the published articles run to about `words` words and a new one to 4,000–6,000, so absolute counts differ by length alone. `brand` is the number of brand mentions; `contrasts_per_article` is the broad count of “X, not Y / rather than / instead of”. Measure all of them on your own published articles. The values below are illustrative round numbers, not a measurement: measure your own published articles and put the averages here.
